original.description: Full-length studio portrait of Wilhelm II in the white full-dress tunic of the Garde du Corps with the eagle-crested parade helmet, sash, stars and neck orders, both hands resting on a drawn sword; a throne, a table bearing a crown and a palm behind him. The print carries the studio imprint 'Originalaufnahme der Hofphotos. Reichard & Lindner, Berlin 1905' and 'Verlag von Gustav Liersch & Co, Berlin'.
original.archive: Deutsches Historisches Museum (LeMO), object 95007746 — via Wikimedia Commons; issued as a postcard by Gustav Liersch & Co, Berlin
original.original_dimensions: 284 × 747 (the Commons copy, which is a narrow crop of the same sitting)

colorization.status: ok — label 'colorized (AI-assisted)'. Documented colours: the white tunic, gilt eagle helmet and black lacquered boots of the Garde du Corps; gold shoulder cords and aiguillette. Two things for the image review (sand-y0u.7): the individual stars and ribbon colours are the colorizer's reading rather than taken from a reference, and this colorization shows a wider framing than the Commons file recorded above, so it derives from a fuller reproduction of the same Reichard & Lindner sitting whose particular scan is not identified.

caption: Wilhelm II in the white full dress of the Garde du Corps, photographed by the court photographers Reichard & Lindner in 1905 and sold as a postcard — the Kaiser as he wished to be seen. Colorized (AI-assisted) from a public-domain photograph.
credit: Original photograph: Reichard & Lindner, Berlin, 1905; published by Gustav Liersch & Co; Deutsches Historisches Museum via Wikimedia Commons; public domain. Colorization: Sandtable, AI-assisted, 2026.
notes: Replaces the monochrome 284 × 747 Commons original filed in PR #64, which was too small to generate WebP variants or carry a card (sand-y0u.14). Colorized version provided by Dave 2026-08-23 at 936 × 1681.
